rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.quote: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.summary: Landlords can only evict tenants from units covered by the Rent Ordinance if they have one of the seventeen just cause reasons listed in the ordinance, and the just cause must be the dominant motive for the eviction.
rules.coverage_text: rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance; some tenancies exempt from rent increase limitations are still subject to eviction provisions, including tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where rent is regulated by another government agency
rules.exemption_note: tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from rent increase limitations but still subject to eviction provisions
rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, the landlord may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability
